I created two files. I couldn't build or run anything in this session, so the image is untested.

**Files created**
- `Dockerfile`
- `.dockerignore`

**How it works**
- **Base image:** `denoland/deno:debian-2.5.6`. Your `deno.lock` uses a format that needs Deno 2.3 or newer. You can change the version with the `DENO_VERSION` build argument. I picked 2.5.6 from memory and didn't check that this tag exists, so that's the first thing to look at if the build fails to pull the base image.
- **Extra packages:**
  - `git`: the bot won't start outside a git repo.
  - `nodejs`: to run the Claude Code CLI that ships inside the Claude Agent SDK package.
  - `procps` and `iproute2`: the `/system-*` commands call `ps`, `ip` and `ss`.
  - `tini`: cleans up child processes and passes stop signals to the bot.
- **Dependencies** are downloaded and cached at build time with `deno install`. It then runs `deno run --allow-all index.ts`, the same as `deno task start`. Anything you add after the image name in `docker run` (such as `--category myproject`) is passed to the bot as flags.
- **User:** it runs as the image's built-in `deno` user rather than root. I gave that user a home folder so Claude Code has somewhere to keep its `~/.claude` data.
- **Settings:**
  - `WORK_DIR=/app/workspace`: mount your project there.
  - `DOCKER_CONTAINER=true`: the code already checks for this.
  - The optional `GIT_COMMIT` build argument is used by the update checker.
- **Things the code requires that shaped the setup:**
  - The app reads `deno.json` and `.env` from the folder it's started in, and looks up the git repo and branch there. So it runs from `/app`, and the build runs `git init -b main` there.
  - Because of that, the Discord category defaults to `app` unless you set `CATEGORY_NAME`.
  - Git's ownership check is turned off for all folders, so a mounted project owned by a different user still works with `/git`.
- **`.dockerignore`** keeps `.env`, `.git`, `.bot-data`, tests and the setup scripts out of the image. Secrets should be passed when you start the container, for example with `--env-file .env`.

**To use it** (the same commands are in the comment at the top of the Dockerfile):
```bash
docker build --build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -t claude-code-discord .
docker run -d --env-file .env \
  -v /path/to/project:/app/workspace \
  -v claude-bot-data:/app/.bot-data \
  -v claude-home:/home/deno/.claude \
  claude-code-discord
```
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is required in the container, because you can't run `claude /login` there.

**Not checked:** I didn't confirm that the SDK's Claude CLI starts correctly under Deno inside the container. The first real `/claude` prompt will show whether it does.
